- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert — cap forecast peak and introduce early downward slope.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.3) and price is trending up, model often overestimates momentum — reduce forecast slope slightly or add early correction.
- Model frequently underestimates downward moves in low-sentiment periods — increase forecast sensitivity to recent negative sentiment.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to lag true price by 1–3 days — adjust forecast to align with recent 7–14 day trend, not just 18-day history.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings), model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecast with weighted average of 3–5 day sentiment and price trends.
- If true outcome is significantly below forecast (e.g., > 5% gap), check if sentiment was positive recently — if so, reduce forecast by 10–20% to account for sentiment misalignment.
- If true outcome is significantly above forecast (e.g., > 5% gap), check if sentiment was negative recently — if so, increase forecast by 10–20% to account for sentiment misalignment.
